Fidelity: the main goal (exit) pays 1.0 from either u0 or u1, and the optional preference is encoded as a one-time 0.2 bonus on the first toggle, so toggle-then-exit totals 1.2 > 1.0 for exit alone — exactly the 'preferably' semantics, with exit-only runs still fully rewarded. The RM correctly ignores setup-only exit conditions (siren silence, box holding), which the stated task does not mention. Structure: FINAL_STATES header is present and nonempty (u2), u2 is declared in STATES and is accepting/absorbing ((u2, else) -> u2 only); all states are reachable (u0 -> u2 directly, u0 -> u1 -> u2). Ordered transition coverage is sound: guards within each state are mutually exclusive and exhaustive — u0 handles toggle/exit/else, u1 handles exit/else, u2 absorbs; the per-state else self-loops cover all irrelevant propositions (siren_ringing, holding_box, box_fell) and any co-occurring combinations, so no stray event causes an unintended transition. Persistent/event distinction is correct: the event switch_toggled is used as a one-shot trigger and the persistent conditions are not misused as events; no regressions are needed since the task has no decaying obligations (a toggle need not be maintained). Reward safety: the 0.2 bonus is structurally bounded — re-toggles in u1 fall to else with no reward, so no accumulation farming; maximum episode total is 1.2; the reward is as dense as the task allows (terminal exit reward plus the single natural milestone). Edge cases behave sensibly: a toggle on the final step-limit step still fires u0->u1 with 0.2 but no exit reward, and exit always ends in u2. Minor note only: the '!at_exit' conjunct in the u0 toggle guard is redundant given the environment constraint that switch_toggled and at_exit never co-occur, but it is harmless and creates no coverage gap. Format matches the paper's RM syntax (headers, (u, phi) -> u' edges, (u, phi, u') -> r rewards, boolean operators, else defaults).
